newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Suspected tribal rebels kill Bangladesh policeman.
newsitem.headline: Suspected tribal rebels kill Bangladesh policeman.

text.p: Suspected tribal guerrillas shot and killed a police officer on Sunday in Bangladesh's southeastern Chittagong Hill Tracts, police said.

They said gunmen ambushed police sub-inspector Shafiqul Islam, who was riding a motorbike in the insurgent-infested Kalapahar pass in Bandarban hill district. He died on the spot and his companion was wounded, police said without giving further details.
Guerrillas, known as Santi Bahini (peace force), have been fighting a bush war in the 14,200 sq km (5,500 sq-mile) Hill Tracts bordering India and Burma since 1973 seeking political autonomy.
They also want some 300,000 Bengali-speaking settlers expelled from the area.
Officials say more than 8,000 civilians, rebels and soldiers have been killed in the protracted insurgency, which has also forced thousands of tribal families to flee to northeast India.
The tribal insurgents abducted and killed 30 Bengali-speaking settlers on September 10.
